observations: Photo 0 shows a complete-looking engine bay/engine assembly on a stand or floor, with visible intake/exhaust plumbing, fuel/ignition components, and a serpentine belt/pulley system.
Photo 0 includes a visible alternator and multiple sensors/solenoids on the top/side of the engine.
Photo 1 shows the same engine from a different angle, with the alternator, crank pulley area, and more of the top harness/sensors visible.
No clear engine make/model badge, casting number, or nameplate is readable in either photo.
The seller’s text says “Hyundai kia engine 4cylinder”, but the photos do not show a readable Hyundai/Kia engine code.

claims.evidence: Photos show a 4-cylinder-looking engine layout but no readable Hyundai/Kia branding or engine code/casting number to confirm make/model or cylinder count.

risks.risk: Exact engine variant (Hyundai vs Kia, and which engine family) is not identifiable from the photos; wrong variant can cause fitment and ECU/sensor mismatch.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the engine ID plate/casting numbers (block head casting) and/or the VIN/engine code label.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic used 4-cylinder engine assembly with unknown variant (worst-case: may require parts/rewiring/ECU matching).

risks.risk: Condition/working status is unknown (could be seized, leaking, or missing parts).
risks.proof: Video of a cold start (or compression test results) plus photos of all accessories and hoses present.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not proven working (worst-case: treat as for spares/needs overhaul).

risks.risk: Mileage and service history are unknown; internal wear (timing chain/belt, bearings) may be high.
risks.proof: Service records or odometer/engine code that ties to mileage; also photo of timing cover/chain condition if accessible.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as high-wear used engine (worst-case: timing/major service likely).

risks.risk: Missing or swapped components (injectors, sensors, alternator, AC compressor, crank pulley) can be present but not fully verifiable.
risks.proof: Photo checklist: underside and both sides showing all sensors/connectors, and a full inventory of included parts.
risks.if_unproven: Priced assuming possible missing/incorrect accessories (worst-case: buyer may need replacements).

risks.risk: Compatibility with buyer’s vehicle (mounts, wiring harness, ECU, starter location) is unknown.
risks.proof: Buyer’s car make/model/year/engine + seller confirmation of exact engine code and included ECU/harness (if applicable).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as requiring compatibility verification (worst-case: may not bolt in without extra parts).

proof_requests: Clear photo of the engine code/ID plate or casting numbers on the block/head (both sides if possible).
Video of engine start (or compression test/leak-down test results).
Photos showing the full accessory set included (alternator, starter, AC compressor, power steering pump, sensors) and what is missing.
Photo of the timing system area (timing chain/belt cover) or proof it was recently serviced.
Confirm the exact Hyundai/Kia model/engine family the engine came from (and provide the donor vehicle details).
response.reason: The photos show an engine assembly but do not provide readable make/model/engine code or proof of working condition, so a reliable worst-case price cannot be set without the decisive identifiers and test/start evidence.
